overview_text: This map covers all 26 health zones in the study area, on a basemap of today's OSM main roads, rivers and towns. Grey shows where buildings were already mapped on 1 April. Orange shows buildings added since then that are still in OSM. Most additions are concentrated in and around Bunia, Rwampara and Rimba, and in the north-east around Kambala and Rethy. The black squares mark the zoomed views below.

notes.html: Each frame is a snapshot of OpenStreetMap on that date, rebuilt from the full edit history. A building counts as present on date T if one of its versions was created on or before T and replaced or deleted after T. The date a building appears is the date it was mapped, not the date it was built. The roads, rivers and place names behind the footprints come from today's OSM, so some roads may themselves have been mapped during the period.

notes.h: Why this isn't an epidemic map
notes.html: When a zone gets mapped depends on Tasking Manager priorities, the order tasks were opened in, and how many volunteers and validators were working. It does not depend on how intense transmission was. Some zones lost buildings overall, for example Drodro, Damas, Tchomia and Fataki, because validators deleted or replaced old low-quality footprints. Net counts therefore understate the work done. Read Added and Removed together, and compare with the case curves before concluding that mapping followed the epidemic.

• An offline synthetic test reproduced the expected counts: Bunia 200→486, Rwampara 300→1,432.
  • For 3 tiles, counts rebuilt from the full history matched ohsome /stats/features/count exactly (0.00%) at 28-day steps from 1 Apr to 15 Nov.
  • For a 0.05° box in central Bunia on 1 Oct, the rebuilt count was 55,668 buildings and the stats endpoint gave 55,668.
  • Deleted buildings: in API v2.1.1, deleted versions already end at their deletion time, not at the 2222-01-01 placeholder the docs describe. The script's extra deletion step therefore changes nothing.
  • Weekly check on the busiest tiles: Bunia, Rwampara, Mongbwalu, Kambala, Rimba, Drodro and an Aungba tile. Counts rebuilt from the history matched /stats/features/count exactly (0.00%) at every one of the 34 weekly dates from 1 Apr to 21 Nov.

• Data: ohsome API v2 (2.1.1), extraction endpoints, filter building=* and geometry:polygon, 1 Apr to 21 Nov 2026, weekly frames.
  • Tiles: all 127 tiles of 0.15° are included. The full history to 15 Nov was downloaded on 16 Nov, the last 5 tiles (covering part of Aungba) on 21 Nov, and edits from 15 to 21 Nov were added on 21 Nov, one request per tile. Only 5 building edits were made in the whole area in that week.
  • Zones: GRID3 COD Ituri Geospatial Data Layers, fourth rapid update (Sept 2026), health-zone layer. A zone is included if at least 25% of it falls inside HOT's ~22,750 km² priority area.
  • Campaign tag: a changeset counts if its tags contain eboladrc2026, which also matches #eboladrc2026mapping. Nearly every addition carries the tag.

• Figures are cumulative confirmed cases and deaths by health zone, taken from the tables in 17 INSP daily SitReps (N°59 of 13 Jul to N°189 of 19 Nov).
  • June and July points for Bunia, Rwampara, Mongbwalu and Nyankunde come from WHO Disease Outbreak News, which gives cases only.
  • Probable cases are not included.
  • INSP lists 493 Ituri deaths under à ventiler (not yet assigned to a zone), so deaths by zone are undercounted.
  • The outbreak has spread well beyond the mapped area: Nord-Kivu has 3,040 cases and Haut-Uélé 541.

• The HDX weekly OSM export for building counts on a given date.
  • The ohsomeNow totals for #eboladrc2026, compared with the Campaign-tagged column.
  • The GRID3 gap analysis figure (about 1,200 settlements more than 1 km from any OSM settlement). No source for it has been found.
